Situations / Jean-Claude — Grung Expansion

Jean-Claude — Grung Expansion

Situation

Simone Tabarnack is actively looking for Jean-Claude as part of a broader Grung expansion she is architecting. Jean-Claude knows the Grung slave system from the handler side, ran from it, and does not yet understand how far Simone’s reach has extended.

Current State

Blue-caste scouts have reached outer Midchain waters under trade cover, farther than the Grung have operated in years. One raid hit a small coastal settlement; a second overextended and failed. Rumour of unusually distant Grung raids is moving through fishing communities.

Simone does not know Jean-Claude’s location. She knows he is alive and outside the Verdant Teeth. Rook was her buyer for Grung hunting toxin into the Central Strait; with Rook gone silent, her operative asked the wrong questions in Tidefall and exposed the supply channel at one end. Verity Hollowell is positioned to hear the wrong-shaped inquiry.

Toy Fields

FieldValue
VerbHunts. Simone expands territory and searches for the deserter who understands the system’s failure points.
Unstable ConditionThe slave-soldier program is tactically useful but breaking down faster than Karath can replace captives. The Calveno raid is the operation that fills the gap — and proves Simone can reach anywhere.
ConsequenceGrung raids push closer, Tidefall suspicion rises, and Jean-Claude’s past becomes an active operational liability. After Calveno, it becomes a personal indictment: he understands everything that was done, and he was in the city when it happened.
Link of RelevanceJean-Claude’s terminal node is Sorn: Simone, Pell, the Botukuri household, and the slave system concentrate there. Calveno is the moment the distance between him and that node collapses.

Narrative Devices

  • Loaded Gun: Simone’s Rook toxin channel is burned at Tidefall; Verity Hollowell is positioned to hear the wrong-shaped inquiry.
  • Foreshadowing: Sideways looks at Felix Aho’s stall, distant raid rumours, blue-caste scouts under trade cover.
  • Clock: Each world tick can move the scout circuit closer or force Simone to accelerate because the slave-soldier math is failing.
  • Reversal Potential: The Vaka know Gold-caste divisions; the Grung order is less unified than it looks from below.

Key Facts

  • Simone is gold-marked and commands as expansion warlord under pure-gold leadership.
  • She is looking for Jean-Claude as an operational loose end, not family sentiment.
  • Karath has six confirmed vethka hulls on the expanded raid circuit, each carrying fourteen crew and four tons of captive cargo.
  • Slave soldiers are breaking down and sometimes turning on handlers mid-raid.
  • Jean-Claude understands the program’s failure point because he ran slave-handling operations on Sorn before deserting.
  • The Calveno raid uses Dravosi patrol gaps, sewer extraction routes, and summoned Slaad as a distraction. This is what Simone built the western supply chain to fund.

Involved Parties

  • Jean-Claude Tabarnack — blue-caste deserter; dangerous because he knows the system
  • Simone Tabarnack — sister; gold-marked expansion commander; looking for him as a loose end
  • Grung Clans — public face of the threat
  • Verdant Teeth — slave economy and terminal region; Pell died here

Locations

  • Verdant Teeth — slave economy and terminal region
  • Sorn — Botukuri home, largest enslaved population, Pell’s death site, Jean-Claude’s terminal node
  • Drowned Maw area — outer Midchain scout circuit territory

Timeline

  • Jean-Claude deserts after freeing slaves; Pell is tortured for 31 days and dies beneath Sorn.
  • 2026-05-16 world tick: blue-caste scouts reach outer Midchain; one raid succeeds, one fails.
  • Session 02: Beaumont uses a Truth Stone; Jean-Claude admits former kinsmen hunted him but does not mention Simone.
  • 2026-05-19 world tick: Simone’s operative exposes the Rook toxin channel while asking questions in Tidefall.

Triggers

  • Party enters Midchain waters inside the extended scout circuit
  • Jean-Claude’s wariness around birds or Aarakocra becomes visible
  • Grung presence appears in a port under trade cover
  • Simone receives a confirmed sighting
  • The slave-soldier program breaks down badly enough to force acceleration

Blocks

  • Distance and speed: the party can outrun delayed scout reports
  • Jean-Claude develops a working cover identity
  • Dravosi ports constrain overt Grung action
  • Vaka or Rattkin contacts help interpret Grung movement before Simone closes

Consequences

  • Simone gets a sighting: redirects scouts and escalates from circuit search to targeted pursuit
  • Rook channel fully burns: Tidefall factor networks connect Grung toxin, Rook, and non-Crown inquiries
  • Party reaches Sorn: Jean-Claude confronts the slave system, Simone, and Pell’s death at the same node
  • Ignored: raids normalize farther west; Felix Aho’s stall becomes a target for local backlash

Open Questions

  • Does Simone want Jean-Claude dead, recaptured, exposed, or used?
  • Which Gold faction benefits from Jean-Claude returning?
  • Can the party weaponize the slave-soldier program’s failure before Sorn?
  • Does Jean-Claude tell the party Simone supplied Rook’s toxin?

DM Notes

Pell Flashback Use

Play Pell warm first: she made Jean-Claude feel seen, not useful. The crack is when she talks about slaves who will never get out. She does not cry; she gets very still.

Sample lines:

  • “Where I’m from, it’s different. Not better, just — different. That’s enough, isn’t it?”
  • “You already knew. You just needed someone to say it out loud.”
  • “I’m not telling you what to do. I’m just telling you what I’ve seen.”

Death fact: Pell died in a cell beneath Sorn after 31 days of torture for names. She did not know whether Jean-Claude made it out.

Felix Aho Read-Aloud

Read Aloud

The dock market moves the way water moves — around obstacles, filling gaps. A smell pulls attention before you see the stall: sweet and sharp and wrong. Behind the counter a green grung barely three feet tall wraps a parcel for a harbour porter with quick, unhurried hands. He looks up; wide amber eyes move across the group the way a man reads a document. He smiles warmly. His eyes do not stop working. “Well. You look hungry.”

Session Log

SessionDevelopment
World Tick 2026-05-16Blue-caste scouts pushed into outer Midchain under trade cover. One raid landed; a second overextended and returned empty. Raid rumour begins moving through fishing communities.
Session 02Beaumont used a Truth Stone on Jean-Claude. Jean-Claude truthfully said former kinsmen hunted him and he was not there on anyone’s behalf. Beaumont did not ask about Simone; Jean-Claude did not mention her.
World Tick 2026-05-19Rook was Simone’s toxin buyer. With Rook silent, Simone sent a blue-caste operative to check his last route. The operative asked wrong-shaped questions in Tidefall and exposed the supply channel at one end.
World Update — Session 03 (Cold)Roll: 20 — Full Success. A vethka crew under trade cover raided a western Midchain fishing settlement — closer to the Central Strait than Grung have operated in a generation. Fourteen captives, zero crew casualties, no witnesses who can identify them as Grung. Slave-soldier pipeline replenished. The scout circuit now operates at a range where Calveno-bound shipping routes intersect their patrol area. Hook strength: Ripple — fishing communities in the western Midchain are now reporting unusual raiders; Felix Aho’s stall in Calveno may hear about it through trade contacts.
Session 04Jean-Claude led the Grung sewer investigation. Executed a purple Grung handler who called him “traitor” and “dissident” and confirmed [[simone-tabarnack

World Update — Session 04

Roll: 6 — Partial (low end) The purple handler who recognized Jean-Claude as a defector is dead. The two blue tunnel Grung are dead. Felix is captured. The critical identification — that a Grung defector was part of the team that hit Le Paludi — died with the handler. The remaining purple handlers at the 4 active sites learned about the operational loss through internal channels (missing handler, destroyed ship, no returning patrol), but their communications carry only the compromise, not who did it. Simone’s command structure knows the Calveno operation was partially hit; they do not know Jean-Claude was involved. His anonymity holds for now. The window closes if: Felix talks to the wrong person, another Grung sighting of JC occurs during the next engagement, or the Tidefall toxin inquiry (already burned) gets cross-referenced with a Central Strait defector report. None of those have fired yet.
